title: Sum the Valid Numbers
statement:
Some of the values in a line are numbers and some are junk. Add up the numbers and count the junk, without letting one bad value stop the program.

The input is one line with 1 to 100 tokens, separated by spaces. Tokens use only lowercase letters, the digits 0 to 9, `-`, and `.`. A token is valid when it is a whole integer: an optional minus sign followed by digits only, like `12` or `-4`. Anything else, such as `apple`, `2.5`, `7x`, or a lone `-`, is invalid. Every valid integer is between -1000000 and 1000000. Try to parse each token as an integer and handle the parse error for the ones that fail.

Print two numbers on one line, separated by a space: the sum of the valid integers, then how many tokens were invalid. When no token is valid the sum is `0`.

Input:

```text
4 apple 10 -3 2.5 x9
```

Expected output:

```text
11 3
```
hints: Keep two running values, a sum and a count of bad tokens, and visit every token once.
Put the parse inside error handling. When it succeeds add the number, and when it fails add one to the count and move on.
